title: Austria's gas
hook: How Austria ran on Siberian gas, then stopped.
notes: Russian share of Austrian gas imports ≈ 80% in 2021, peaking near 98% in late 2023 (Austrian ministry for climate and energy). Gazprom halted deliveries to OMV in Nov 2024; OMV terminated the contract in Dec 2024; transit through Ukraine ended 1 Jan 2025. Pipeline routes schematic.

scenes.title: Baumgarten
scenes.text: A village on the March river, east of Vienna, is one of Central Europe's biggest gas hubs. For decades, Soviet and then Russian gas arrived here first.

scenes.title: A 4,000 km pipe
scenes.text: Gas from West Siberia crossed Russia, Ukraine and Slovakia to reach Austria. Austria was the first Western country to sign a gas deal with the Soviet Union, in 1968.

scenes.title: Deeper dependence
scenes.text: Even after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Russian gas made up most of Austria's imports, close to 98% at one point in late 2023, largely because of a long-term OMV contract running to 2040.

scenes.title: The tap closes
scenes.text: In November 2024 Gazprom stopped deliveries to OMV, which cancelled the contract. On 1 January 2025, transit through Ukraine ended. Austria now imports via Germany and Italy, including Norwegian gas and LNG.
